newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Tribunal wants arrest of Bosnia war crimes suspects.
newsitem.headline: Tribunal wants arrest of Bosnia war crimes suspects.

text.p: The U.N. criminal tribunal for the former Yugoslavia on Wednesday called for the immediate arrest of four indicted war crimes suspects believed to be working as policemen in northwest Bosnia.

"The fact that four persons indicted by the tribunal since 1995 are reportedly holding public law enforcement positions and were easily located by the media is another example of blatant disregard for international law," it said in a statement.

The four, named as Mladen Radic, Miroslav Kvocka, Nedjelko Timarac and Zeljko Mejakic, were indicted by the tribunal in 1995, when warrants were issued for their arrest and forwarded to the appropriate local authorities.

"The tribunal calls upon all the parties, including Republika Srpka, to comply with their obligation to arrest immediately the persons indicted and to discharge all their other obligations under Dayton."
A U.N. report dated October 27 and faxed to Reuters on Tuesday said the men were serving as police officers in the Serb-controlled Prijedor area.
Radic and Kvocka were indicted for crimes against civilian prisoners at Omarska detention camp near Prijedor and Timarac for crimes at Keraterm camp, also near Prijedor.

Mejakic, whose picture appears on a war criminals poster, is believed to have been one of the commanders of Omarska camp and currently works at Omarska police station, 30 km (20 miles) east of Prijedor.

"The fact that they are still walking free is a clear breach of the provisions of the Security Council Resolution establishing the tribunal and of the Dayton Peace Agreement. If true, the fact that they are holding public offices is an additional breach of the Dayton Agreement," the tribunal said.
